claim: Let \(C_n\), \(n\ge3\), be the cycle and let player \(i\) choose \(x_i\ge0\) with payoff \(b(x_{i-1}+x_i+x_{i+1})-cx_i\), where \(b\in C^2([0,\infty))\), \(b'>0\), \(b''<0\), and \(q>0\) is the unique solution of \(b'(q)=c\). The pure Nash equilibria are exactly: (i) fully positive profiles periodic with period dividing three, hence uniform \(x_i=q/3\) when \(3\nmid n\), and repetitions of any positive triple \((a,b,d)\) with \(a+b+d=q\) when \(3\mid n\); or (ii) profiles with zeros whose cyclic blocks are singleton active blocks \(S=(q)\) and double active blocks \(D(a)=(a,q-a)\), \(0<a<q\), separated by zero gaps of length one or two. A length-two zero gap is permitted only between singleton active blocks; across a length-one gap between consecutive double blocks \(D(a),D(b)\), the parameters must satisfy \(b\ge a\). The resulting equilibrium set has maximal semialgebraic dimension \[d_{\max}(n)=\begin{cases}\max\{2,n/3-2\},&n\equiv0\pmod3,\\(n-4)/3,&n\equiv1\pmod3,\\(n-2)/3,&n\equiv2\pmod3.\end{cases}\]

assumptions: homogeneous strictly concave benefit b and linear cost c
scientific_limitations_integrity.integrity: Self-contained analytic proof; no external certification or independent validation claimed.
limitations: no robustness claim for heterogeneous agents, directed edges, weighted edges, or bounded effort
literature novelty is limited to the explicit cycle block classification and dimension invariant; broader unsearched sources remain a risk

title: Exact equilibrium-set dimension law for cycle public-goods games
